      "verbatim_text": "8.2.10 LinIf_SetTrcvWakeupMode\n[SWS_LinIf_00550] Definition of API function LinIf_SetTrcvWakeupMode\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Lin_01589\n⌈\nService Name\nLinIf_SetTrcvWakeupMode\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType LinIf_SetTrcvWakeupMode (\nNetworkHandleType Channel,\nLinTrcv_TrcvWakeupModeType LinTrcvWakeupMode\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x0b\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant\nChannel\nIdentification of the LIN channel\nParameters (in)\nLinTrcvWakeupMode\nRequested transceiver wake up reason.\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: The call of the LIN Transceiver Driver’s API service has\nreturned E_OK.\nE_NOT_OK: The call of the LIN Transceiver Driver’s API service\nhas returned E_NOT_OK or channel or mode parameter is invalid.\nDescription\nThis API enables, disables and clears the notification for wakeup events on the addressed\nnetwork\nAvailable via\nLinIf.h\n⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00551] ⌈This API shall enable, disable or clear the notification for wake\nup events on the addressed network by calling the underlying function LinTrcv_-\nSetWakeupMode(LinNetwork, TrcvWakeupMode).⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00595] ⌈If development error detection is enabled and an invalid value for\nChannel is given, the function LinIf_SetTrcvWakeupMode shall report LINIF_\nE_NONEXISTENT_CHANNEL to the default error tracer.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00596] ⌈If development error detection is enabled and an invalid value\nfor LinTrcvWakeupMode is given, the function LinIf_SetTrcvWakeupMode shall\nreport LINIF_E_PARAMETER to the default error tracer.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00637] ⌈The function LinIf_SetTrcvWakeupMode is required only if\nat least one LIN channel uses the LIN transceiver driver. This function shall be pre-\ncompile time configurable On/Off by the configuration parameter LinIfTrcvDriver-\nSupported.⌋\nCaveats:\n• The LIN Interface has to be initialized with a call of LinIf_Init before this API\nservice may be called, see [SRS_BSW_00487].\n• The implementation may be e.g. disabling the interrupt source for the wake up.\nIf the interrupt is level triggered a pending interrupt is automatically stored and\nraised after enabling the notification again. It is very important not to lose wake\nup events during the disabled period."
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.2.11 LinIf_GetPIDTable\nThe service LinIf_GetPIDTable is only applicable to LIN slave node (available only\nif the ECU has any LIN slave channel).\n[SWS_LinIf_91002] Definition of API function LinIf_GetPIDTable ⌈\nService Name\nLinIf_GetPIDTable\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType LinIf_GetPIDTable (\nNetworkHandleType Channel,\nLin_FramePidType* PidBuffer,\nuint8* PidBufferLength\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x72\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant\nParameters (in)\nChannel\nIdentification of the LIN channel.\nPidBuffer\nPointer to existing buffer to which the current assigned PID values\nare copied to\nParameters (inout)\nPidBufferLength\nPointer to actual length of provided buffer. After successful return,\nit contains the number of copied PID values.\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: Request has been accepted.\nE_NOT_OK: Request has not been accepted, development or\nproduction error occurred.\n▽\n△\nDescription\nRetrieves all assigned PID values. The order is congruent to the LIN frame index.\nOnly applicable for LIN slave nodes.\nAvailable via\nLinIf.h\n⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00816] ⌈This API shall return the configured PIDs of all frames relevant\nfor the slave node. The order shall be ascending corresponding to the configuration\nparameter LinIfFrameIndex. The value of PidBufferLength shall be updated\nwith the actual number of configured PIDs.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00817] ⌈The returned PID list shall not include the PIDs for MRF and\nSRF.⌋\nRationale: MRF and SRF are always implicitly assigned to each slave node and their\nPIDs shall not be changed (see also [SWS_LinIf_00809]).\n[SWS_LinIf_00828] ⌈If the length of the buffer (provided by parameter PidBuffer-\nLength) is 0, the function shall return the number of configured PIDs of the slave node\nin parameter PidBufferLength, without updating the PID buffer with PIDs.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00818] ⌈If development error detection is enabled and an invalid value\nfor Channel is given, the function LinIf_GetPIDTable shall report LINIF_E_-\nNONEXISTENT_CHANNEL to the default error tracer.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00819] ⌈If development error detection is enabled and an invalid value for\nPidBuffer is given, the function LinIf_GetPIDTable shall raise the development\nerror code LINIF_E_PARAM_POINTER.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00820] ⌈If development error detection is enabled and an invalid value\nfor PidBufferLength is given, the function LinIf_GetPIDTable shall raise the\ndevelopment error code LINIF_E_PARAM_POINTER.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00821] ⌈If development error detection is enabled and length of the buffer\n(provided by parameter PidBufferLength) is smaller than the number of configured\nPIDs of the slave node (except 0, see [SWS_LinIf_00828]), the function LinIf_Get-\nPIDTable shall raise the development error code LINIF_E_PARAMETER.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00859] ⌈The function LinIf_GetPIDTable is only available if the LinIf\nmodule is configured as LIN slave node on at least one channel. In a pure LIN master\nconfiguration, this function is not available. This depends on the configuration parame-\nter LinIfNodeType.⌋"

      "verbatim_text": "8.2.15 LinTp_Init\n[SWS_LinIf_00350] Definition of API function LinTp_Init\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00101, SRS_BSW_00414, SRS_BSW_00416, SRS_BSW_\n00358, SRS_Lin_01540\n⌈\nService Name\nLinTp_Init\nSyntax\nvoid LinTp_Init (\nconst LinTp_ConfigType* ConfigPtr\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x40\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nNon Reentrant\nParameters (in)\nConfigPtr\nPointer to the LIN Transport Protocol configuration.\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nNone\nDescription\nInitializes the LIN Transport Layer.\nAvailable via\nLinIf.h\n⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00427] ⌈The parameter ConfigPtr of the function LinTp_Init is only\nrelevant for the configuration variant VARIANT-POST-BUILD. The parameter Config-\nPtr shall be ignored for the configuration variant VARIANT-PRE-COMPILE and the\nconfiguration variant VARIANT-LINK-TIME.⌋\nThe LIN Interface’s environment shall call the function LinTp_Init before using any\nother LIN TP function.\n[SWS_LinIf_00320] ⌈The function LinTp_Init shall set the state LINTP_INIT and\nsub-state LINTP_CHANNEL_IDLE for each configured channel of the LIN TP channel\nstate-machine.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00681] ⌈The function LinTp_Init shall be pre-compile time config-\nurable On/Off by the configuration parameter LinIfTpSupported.⌋"
    },

      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_LINInterface",

      "verbatim_text": "8.2.16 LinTp_Transmit\n[SWS_LinIf_00351] Definition of API function LinTp_Transmit ⌈\nService Name\nLinTp_Transmit\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType LinTp_Transmit (\nPduIdType TxPduId,\nconst PduInfoType* PduInfoPtr\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x53\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant for different PduIds. Non reentrant for the same PduId.\nTxPduId\nIdentifier of the PDU to be transmitted\nParameters (in)\nPduInfoPtr\nLength of and pointer to the PDU data and pointer to MetaData.\nParameters (inout)\nNone\n▽\n△\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: Transmit request has been accepted.\nE_NOT_OK: Transmit request has not been accepted.\nDescription\nRequests transmission of a PDU.\nAvailable via\nLinIf.h\n⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00326] ⌈The function LinTp_Transmit shall prepare a LIN TP mes-\nsage for transmission.⌋\nThe LIN Interface’s environment shall call the function LinIf_Init for initializing the\nreferenced channel before using the function LinTp_Transmit.\n[SWS_LinIf_00413] ⌈The function LinTp_Transmit shall set the sub-state of the\nreferenced channel to LINTP_CHANNEL_BUSY.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00422] ⌈The function LinTp_Transmit shall convert the N-SDU Id\n(given by the parameter TxPduId) to a specific channel and a destination NAD for\nthe slave. This requirement is only applicable to LIN master nodes.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00584] ⌈The function LinTp_Transmit shall accept a functional trans-\nmission request also when a TP message is currently ongoing on the selected channel.\nThis requirement is only applicable to LIN master nodes.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00616] ⌈If the transmission for a further physical request is triggered while\ntransmission of a previously triggered physical request is ongoing, the LIN Interface\nshall accept the new physical request and drop the old physical request.⌋\nNote: According to the ISO 17987 specifications, the NAD 0x7E shall be used for a\nfunctional transmission request.\n[SWS_LinIf_00586] ⌈The LIN Interface shall use the NAD 0x7E for transmission of\nfunctional requests by LIN master nodes.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00702]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Lin_01564\n⌈When LinTp_Transmit was successful (returned E_OK), the LIN Interface shall\ncall PduR_LinTpTxConfirmation after successful completion or failure (e.g.,\nsince some other schedule table change is currently going on) of required sched-\nule table switch (see [SWS_LinIf_00646], [SWS_LinIf_00642], [SWS_LinIf_00643],\n[SWS_LinIf_00707]), with a negative or positive result. When LinTp_Transmit was\nnot successful, PduR_LinTpTxConfirmation shall not be called.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00878]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Lin_01564\n⌈The function LinTp_Transmit shall return E_NOT_OK when the corresponding\nLinIf_ScheduleRequest call (called from BswM_LinTp_RequestMode resulting\nfrom the LinTp_Transmit call, see [SWS_LinIf_00646] and [SWS_LinIf_00641]) re-\nturned E_NOT_OK for the Schedule Request.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00574] ⌈If development error detection is enabled and the parameter\nPduInfoPtr has an invalid value, the function LinTp_Transmit shall raise the de-\nvelopment error code LINIF_E_PARAM_POINTER.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00576] ⌈If development error detection is enabled and the parameter\nTxPduId has an invalid value, the function LinTp_Transmit shall raise the develop-\nment error code LINIF_E_PARAMETER.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00682] ⌈The function LinTp_Transmit shall be pre-compile time con-\nfigurable On/Off by the configuration parameter LinIfTpSupported.⌋\nCaveats: The LIN Interface has to be initialized with a call of LinIf_Init and\nLinTp_Init before this API service may be called, see [SRS_BSW_00487]."
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.2.1 LinIf_Init\n[SWS_LinIf_00198] Definition of API function LinIf_Init\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00101, SRS_BSW_00416, SRS_BSW_00358, SRS_Lin_-\n01569, SRS_BSW_00414\n⌈\nService Name\nLinIf_Init\nSyntax\nvoid LinIf_Init (\nconst LinIf_ConfigType* ConfigPtr\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x01\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nNon Reentrant\nParameters (in)\nConfigPtr\nPointer to the LIN Interface configuration\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nNone\nDescription\nInitializes the LIN Interface.\nAvailable via\nLinIf.h\n⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00373]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00344, SRS_BSW_00404, SRS_BSW_00405, SRS_BSW_-\n00170\n⌈The function LinIf_Init shall accept a parameter that references to a LIN Interface\nconfiguration descriptor.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00233] ⌈The function LinIf_Init shall set the schedule type NULL_-\nSCHEDULE for each configured channel. This requirement is only applicable to LIN\nmaster nodes.⌋"

      "verbatim_text": "8.2.20 LinIf_CheckWakeup\n[SWS_LinIf_00378] Definition of API function LinIf_CheckWakeup\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Lin_01514, SRS_BSW_00375\n⌈\nService Name\nLinIf_CheckWakeup\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType LinIf_CheckWakeup (\nEcuM_WakeupSourceType WakeupSource\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x60\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant\nParameters (in)\nWakeupSource\nSource device, which initiated the wakeup event: LIN controller or\nLIN transceiver\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: No error has occurred during execution of the API\nE_NOT_OK: An error has occurred during execution of the API or\ninvalid WakeupSource\nDescription\nWill be called when the EcuM has been notified about a wakeup on a specific LIN channel.\nAvailable via\nLinIf.h\n⌋\nThe LIN Interface will recognize the source of the wakeup and thus the destination of\nthis call by the parameter of the function LinIf_CheckWakeup.\n[SWS_LinIf_00503] ⌈The function LinIf_CheckWakeup shall issue the call of func-\ntion Lin_CheckWakeup or LinTrcv_CheckWakeup depending on the given param-\neter WakeupSource.⌋\nNote: It is implementation specific, which controllers and transceivers are queried. LinIf\njust has to find out the exact LIN hardware device.\n[SWS_LinIf_00566] ⌈If development error detection is enabled and the parameter\nWakeupSource has an invalid value, the function LinIf_CheckWakeup shall raise\nthe development error code LINIF_E_PARAM_WAKEUPSOURCE.⌋\nThe function LinIf_CheckWakeup may be called in an interrupt or polling mode."
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.2.3 LinIf_Transmit\n[SWS_LinIf_00201] Definition of API function LinIf_Transmit ⌈\nService Name\nLinIf_Transmit\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType LinIf_Transmit (\nPduIdType TxPduId,\nconst PduInfoType* PduInfoPtr\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x49\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant for different PduIds. Non reentrant for the same PduId.\nTxPduId\nIdentifier of the PDU to be transmitted\nParameters (in)\nPduInfoPtr\nLength of and pointer to the PDU data and pointer to MetaData.\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: Transmit request has been accepted.\nE_NOT_OK: Transmit request has not been accepted.\nDescription\nRequests transmission of a PDU.\nAvailable via\nLinIf.h\n⌋(SRS_Lin_01571)\nNote: TxPduId is the identifier of LIN frame for upper layer (not the LIN protected ID).\nThis parameter is used to determine the corresponding LIN protected ID (PID) and\nimplicitly the LIN Driver instance as well as the corresponding LIN Controller device.\n[SWS_LinIf_00105] ⌈The function LinIf_Transmit shall indicate a request from an\nupper layer to transmit a frame specified by the parameter TxPduId.⌋()\n[SWS_LinIf_00341] ⌈The function LinIf_Transmit shall only mark a Sporadic\nframe (LIN master node) or an Event-triggered frame (LIN slave node) as pend-\ning for transmission and shall ignore other frame types.⌋()\n[SWS_LinIf_00700] ⌈The function LinIf_Transmit shall also return E_OK in case\nthe Pdu belongs to a non-Sporadic frame (LIN master node) or non-Event-trig-\ngered frame (LIN slave node) and LIN Interface is initialized.⌋()\n[SWS_LinIf_00106] ⌈The function LinIf_Transmit shall tolerate repeated invoca-\ntions while the Sporadic frame (LIN master node) or Event-triggered frame\n(LIN slave node) is still pending.⌋()\n[SWS_LinIf_00570] ⌈If development error detection is enabled and the parameter\nPduInfoPtr has an invalid value, the function LinIf_Transmit shall raise the de-\nvelopment error code LINIF_E_PARAM_POINTER.⌋()\n[SWS_LinIf_00575] ⌈If development error detection is enabled and the parameter\nTxPduId has an invalid value, the function LinIf_Transmit shall raise the develop-\nment error code LINIF_E_PARAMETER.⌋()\n[SWS_LinIf_00719] ⌈LinIf_Transmit() shall return E_NOT_OK in case the LinIf’s\ncurrent schedule is NULL_SCHEDULE. This requirement is only applicable to LIN mas-\nter nodes.⌋()\nCaveats: The LIN Interface has to be initialized with a call of LinIf_Init before this\nAPI service may be called, see [SRS_BSW_00487]."
    },
    {

      "verbatim_text": "8.2.4 LinIf_ScheduleRequest\nThe service LinIf_ScheduleRequest is only applicable to LIN master node (avail-\nable only if the ECU has any LIN master channel).\n[SWS_LinIf_00202] Definition of API function LinIf_ScheduleRequest\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Lin_01564\n⌈\nService Name\nLinIf_ScheduleRequest\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType LinIf_ScheduleRequest (\nNetworkHandleType Channel,\nLinIf_SchHandleType ScheduleTableIdx\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x05\nSync/Async\nAsynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant\nChannel\nChannel index.\nParameters (in)\nScheduleTableIdx\nIndex of the scheduled table\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: Schedule table request has been accepted.\nE_NOT_OK: Schedule table switch request has not been accepted\ndue to one of the following reasons:\n- LIN Interface has not been initialized\n- referenced channel does not exist (identification is out of range)\n- referenced schedule table does not exist (identification is out of\nrange)\n- State is sleep\nDescription\nRequests a schedule table to be executed.\nOnly used for LIN master nodes.\nAvailable via\nLinIf.h\n⌋\nThe schedule tables are configured by the LinIfScheduleTable container in the\nLIN Interface configuration.\n[SWS_LinIf_00389] ⌈The function LinIf_ScheduleRequest shall request the\nschedule table manager to be executed.⌋\nIt is possible that each Channel has multiple schedule tables. Each Channel has a\nset of schedule tables that are selectable at run-time.\n[SWS_LinIf_00563] ⌈If development error detection is enabled and an invalid Chan-\nnel is given, the function LinIf_ScheduleRequest shall raise the development\nerror code LINIF_E_NONEXISTENT_CHANNEL.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00567] ⌈If development error detection is enabled and an invalid sched-\nule table is given or the corresponding Channel is in the state LINIF_CHANNEL_\nSLEEP, the function LinIf_ScheduleRequest shall raise the development error\ncode LINIF_E_SCHEDULE_REQUEST_ERROR.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00858] ⌈The function LinIf_ScheduleRequest is only available if the\nLinIf module is configured as LIN master node on at least one channel. In a pure LIN\nslave configuration, this function is not available. This depends on the configuration\nparameter LinIfNodeType.⌋\nCaveats: The LIN Interface has to be initialized with a call of LinIf_Init before this\nAPI service may be called, see [SRS_BSW_00487]."
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.2.5 LinIf_GotoSleep\n[SWS_LinIf_00204] Definition of API function LinIf_GotoSleep\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Lin_01523\n⌈\nService Name\nLinIf_GotoSleep\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType LinIf_GotoSleep (\nNetworkHandleType Channel\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x06\nSync/Async\nAsynchronous\nReentrancy\nNon Reentrant\nParameters (in)\nChannel\nIdentification of the LIN channel.\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: Request to go to sleep has been accepted or sleep\ntransition is already in progress or controller is already in sleep\nstate\nE_NOT_OK: Request to go to sleep has not been accepted due to\none or more of the following reasons:\n- LIN Interface has not been initialized\n- referenced channel does not exist (identification is out of range)\nDescription\nInitiates a transition into the Sleep Mode on the selected channel.\nAvailable via\nLinIf.h\n⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00488] ⌈The function LinIf_GotoSleep shall initiate a transition into\nsleep mode on the selected Channel. (see [SWS_LinIf_00453], [SWS_LinIf_00597]\nand [SWS_LinIf_00757])⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00564] ⌈If development error detection is enabled and an invalid Chan-\nnel is given, the function LinIf_GotoSleep shall raise the development error code\nLINIF_E_NONEXISTENT_CHANNEL.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00113] ⌈The function LinIf_GotoSleep shall have no effect on the\nchannel referenced by the parameter Channel if the channel is already in the sleep\nstate.⌋\nFor LIN master nodes, the function LinIf_GotoSleep will start the process of putting\nthe cluster into sleep and not do it immediately.\nFor LIN slave nodes, the function LinIf_GotoSleep sets the cluster directly into\nsleep after sleep indication by the master node.\nCaveats: The LIN Interface has to be initialized with a call of LinIf_Init before this\nAPI service may be called, see [SRS_BSW_00487]."
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.2.6 LinIf_Wakeup\n[SWS_LinIf_00205] Definition of API function LinIf_Wakeup\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Lin_01515\n⌈\nService Name\nLinIf_Wakeup\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType LinIf_Wakeup (\nNetworkHandleType Channel\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x07\nSync/Async\nAsynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant\nParameters (in)\nChannel\nIdentification of the LIN channel.\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: Request to wake up has been accepted or the controller is\nnot in sleep state.\nE_NOT_OK: Request to wake up has not been accepted due to\none or more of the following reasons:\n- LIN Interface has not been initialized\n- referenced channel does not exist (identification is out of range)\n- Lin_Wakeup has returned E_NOT_OK\n- Lin_WakeupInternal has returned E_NOT_OK\nDescription\nInitiates the wake up process.\nAvailable via\nLinIf.h\n⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00432] ⌈When the referenced Channel is not in the sleep state, the func-\ntion LinIf_Wakeup will not forward the call to the LIN driver. In this case, it will simu-\nlate a successful wakeup by returning E_OK.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00296] ⌈The function LinIf_Wakeup shall call the function Lin_-\nWakeup of the LIN Driver module to transmit a wake-up request on the selected\nChannel, if the Channel is in the channel state LINIF_CHANNEL_SLEEP and the\nwakeup flag of the selected Channel is not set. (see [SWS_LinIf_00716])⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00713] ⌈The function LinIf_Wakeup shall call the function Lin_Wake-\nupInternal of the LIN Driver module to set selected Channel to the wakeup state,\nif the Channel is in the channel state LINIF_CHANNEL_SLEEP and the wakeup flag\nof the selected Channel is set. (see [SWS_LinIf_00716])⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00714] ⌈The function LinIf_Wakeup shall clear the wakeup flag of the\nselected Channel.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00720] ⌈If the function Lin_Wakeup returns E_NOT_OK, the function\nLinIf_Wakeup shall return E_NOT_OK and not change the status of the wakeup flag.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00721] ⌈If the function Lin_WakeupInternal returns E_NOT_OK, the\nfunction LinIf_Wakeup shall return E_NOT_OK and not change the status of the\nwakeup flag.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00565] ⌈If development error detection is enabled and an invalid Chan-\nnel is given, the function LinIf_Wakeup shall raise the development error code\nLINIF_E_NONEXISTENT_CHANNEL.⌋\nCaveats: The LIN Interface has to be initialized with a call of LinIf_Init before this\nAPI service may be called, see [SRS_BSW_00487]."
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.2.7 LinIf_SetTrcvMode\n[SWS_LinIf_00544] Definition of API function LinIf_SetTrcvMode\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Lin_01584, SRS_Lin_01585, SRS_Lin_01586\n⌈\nService Name\nLinIf_SetTrcvMode\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType LinIf_SetTrcvMode (\nNetworkHandleType Channel,\nLinTrcv_TrcvModeType TransceiverMode\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x08\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant\nChannel\nIdentification of the LIN channel\nParameters (in)\nTransceiverMode\nRequested mode transition\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: Will be returned, if the transceiver state has been changed\nto the requested mode.\nE_NOT_OK: Will be returned, if the transceiver state change has\nfailed or the parameter is out of the allowed range. The previous\nstate has not been changed.\nDescription\nSet the given LIN transceiver to the given mode.\nAvailable via\nLinIf.h\n⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00536] ⌈This service shall call the underlying function LinTrcv_SetOp-\nMode(LinNetwork, OpMode) for the corresponding requested LIN transceiver.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00537] ⌈This API shall be applicable to all LIN transceivers with all values\nindependent if the transceiver hardware supports these modes or not.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00538] ⌈The API LinIf_SetTrcvMode returns the value that is returned\nby LinTrcv_SetOpMode.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00539] ⌈If development error detection is enabled and an invalid value\nfor Channel is given, the function LinIf_SetTrcvMode shall report LINIF_E_-\nNONEXISTENT_CHANNEL to the default error tracer.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00540] ⌈If development error detection is enabled and an invalid mode\nis requested for TransceiverMode, the function LinIf_SetTrcvMode shall report\nLINIF_E_TRCV_INV_MODE to the default error tracer.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00634] ⌈The function LinIf_SetTrcvMode is required only if at least\none LIN channel uses the LIN transceiver driver. This function shall be pre-compile time\nconfigurable On/Off by the configuration parameter LinIfTrcvDriverSupported.⌋\nCaveats: The LIN Interface has to be initialized with a call of LinIf_Init before this\nAPI service may be called, see [SRS_BSW_00487]."

given, the function LinIf_GetTrcvWakeupReason shall report\nLINIF_E_NONEXISTENT_CHANNEL to the default error tracer.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00573] ⌈If development error detection is enabled and the parameter Tr-\ncvWuReasonPtr has an invalid value, the function LinIf_GetTrcvWakeupReason\nshall raise the development error code LINIF_E_PARAM_POINTER.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00572] ⌈If development error detection is enabled and the current mode\nis not LINTRCV_TRCV_MODE_NORMAL, the function LinIf_GetTrcvWakeupReason\nshall report LINIF_E_TRCV_NOT_NORMAL to the default error tracer.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00636] ⌈The function LinIf_GetTrcvWakeupReason is required only\nif at least one LIN channel uses the LIN transceiver driver. This function shall be pre-\ncompile time configurable On/Off by the configuration parameter LinIfTrcvDriver-\nSupported.⌋\nCaveats:\n• The LIN Interface has to be initialized with a call of LinIf_Init before this API\nservice may be called, see [SRS_BSW_00487].\n• Please be aware, that if more than one network is available, each network may\nreport a different wake up reason. This API has a“per network” view and does not\nvote the more important reason or sequence internally. The same may be true if\ne.g. one transceiver controls the power supply and the other is just powered or\nun-powered. Then one may be able to return LINTRCV_WU_POWER_ON, whereas\nthe other may state e.g. LINTRCV_WU_RESET.\nIt is up to the EcuM to decide how to handle that wake up information."
    },

    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_LINIF_SECTION_8_3_1_2_Lin_CheckWakeup",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_LINDriver",
      "source_page": 42,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "8.3.1.2 Lin_CheckWakeup\n[SWS_Lin_00160] Definition of API function Lin_CheckWakeup ⌈\nService Name\nLin_CheckWakeup\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType Lin_CheckWakeup (\nuint8 Channel\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x0a\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nNon Reentrant\nParameters (in)\nChannel\nLIN channel to be addressed\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: API call has been accepted\nE_NOT_OK: API call has not been accepted\nDescription\nThis function checks if a wakeup has occurred on the addressed LIN channel.\nAvailable via\nLin.h\n⌋\nThere are two methods in which wake up detection shall happen, one is from LIN\ncontroller hardware [Micro peripheral device] and/or another from LinTranceiver.\n[SWS_Lin_00098]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00375, SRS_Lin_01563\n⌈The function Lin_CheckWakeup shall evaluate the wakeup on the addressed LIN\nchannel. When a wake-up event on the addressed LIN channel (e.g. RxD pin has\nconstant low level) is detected, the function Lin_CheckWakeup shall notify the ECU\nState Manager module immediately via the EcuM_SetWakeupEvent and the Lin Inter-\nface module via LinIf_WakeupConfirmation callback function.⌋\n[SWS_Lin_00251] ⌈If development error detection for the LIN module is enabled:\nif the channel parameter is invalid, the function Lin_CheckWakeup shall raise the\ndevelopment error LIN_E_INVALID_CHANNEL otherwise (if DET is disabled) return\nE_NOT_OK.⌋\n[SWS_Lin_00107] ⌈If development error detection for the LIN module is enabled: if the\nfunction Lin_CheckWakeup is called before the LIN module was initialized, the function\nLin_CheckWakeup shall raise the development error LIN_E_UNINIT.⌋"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_LINIF_SECTION_8_3_1_LinIf_WakeupConfirmation",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_LINInterface",
      "source_page": 98,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "8.3.1 LinIf_WakeupConfirmation\n[SWS_LinIf_00715] Definition of callback function LinIf_WakeupConfirmation ⌈\nService Name\nLinIf_WakeupConfirmation\nSyntax\nvoid LinIf_WakeupConfirmation (\nEcuM_WakeupSourceType WakeupSource\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x61\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant\nParameters (in)\nWakeupSource\nSource device which initiated the wakeup event: LIN controller or\nLIN transceiver\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nNone\nDescription\nThe LIN Driver or LIN Transceiver Driver will call this function to report the wake up source after\nthe successful wakeup detection during CheckWakeup or after power on by bus.\nAvailable via\nLinIf.h\n⌋()\n[SWS_LinIf_00716] ⌈The function LinIf_WakeupConfirmation shall set the\nwakeup flag for the channel depending on the given parameter WakeupSource. The\nwakeup flags shall be provided for each channel.⌋()\n[SWS_LinIf_00717] ⌈If development error detection is enabled and the parameter\nWakeupSource has an invalid value, the function LinIf_WakeupConfirmation\nshall raise the development error code LINIF_E_PARAM_WAKEUPSOURCE.⌋()"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_LINIF_SECTION_8_3_2_LinIf_HeaderIndication",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_LINInterface",
      "source_page": 114,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "8.3.2 LinIf_HeaderIndication\nThe callback function LinIf_HeaderIndication is only applicable for LIN slave\nnode.\n[SWS_LinIf_91004] Definition of callback function LinIf_HeaderIndication ⌈\nService Name\nLinIf_HeaderIndication\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType LinIf_HeaderIndication (\nNetworkHandleType Channel,\nLin_PduType* PduPtr\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x78\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant for different Channels. Non reentrant for the same Channel.\nParameters (in)\nChannel\nIdentification of the LIN channel\nParameters (inout)\nPduPtr\nPointer to PDU providing the received PID and pointer to the SDU\ndata buffer as in parameter. Upon return, the length, checksum\ntype and frame response type are received as out parameter. If\nthe frame response type is LIN_FRAMERESPONSE_TX, then\nthe SDU data buffer contains the transmission data.\nParameters (out)\nNone\n▽\n△\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: Request has been accepted.\nE_NOT_OK: Request has not been accepted, development or\nproduction error occurred.\nDescription\nThe LIN Driver will call this function to report a received LIN header. This function is only\napplicable for LIN slave nodes (available only if the ECU has any LIN slave channel).\nAvailable via\nLinIf.h\n⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00843] ⌈If development error detection is enabled and an invalid value for\nChannel is given, the function LinIf_HeaderIndication shall report LINIF_E_-\nNONEXISTENT_CHANNEL to the default error tracer.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00844] ⌈If development error detection is enabled and the parameter\nPduPtr has an invalid value, the function LinIf_HeaderIndication shall raise the\ndevelopment error code LINIF_E_PARAM_POINTER.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00845] ⌈If development error detection is enabled, the PID is evaluated\nand rated to belong to a transmit frame and the parameter PduPtr->SduPtr has an\ninvalid value, the function LinIf_HeaderIndication shall raise the development\nerror code LINIF_E_PARAM_POINTER.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00863] ⌈The function LinIf_HeaderIndication is only available if the\nLinIf module is configured as LIN slave node on at least one channel. In a pure LIN\nmaster configuration, this function is not available. This depends on the configuration\nparameter LinIfNodeType.⌋"
    },
    {

      "verbatim_text": "8.3.3 LinIf_RxIndication\nThe callback function LinIf_RxIndication is only applicable for LIN slave node.\n[SWS_LinIf_91005] Definition of callback function LinIf_RxIndication ⌈\nService Name\nLinIf_RxIndication\nSyntax\nvoid LinIf_RxIndication (\nNetworkHandleType Channel,\nuint8* Lin_SduPtr\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x79\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\n▽\n△\nReentrancy\nReentrant for different Channels. Non reentrant for the same Channel.\nChannel\nIdentification of the LIN channel\nParameters (in)\nLin_SduPtr\nPointer to pointer to a shadow buffer or memory mapped LIN\nHardware receive buffer where the current SDU is stored. This\npointer is only valid if the response is received.\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nNone\nDescription\nThe LIN Driver will call this function to report a successfully received response and provides the\nreception data to the LIN Interface. This function is only applicable for LIN slave nodes\n(available only if the ECU has any LIN slave channel).\nAvailable via\nLinIf.h\n⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00848] ⌈If no header of a receive frame has been indicated before (no re-\nsponse reception is expected), the function LinIf_RxIndication shall return with-\nout further action.⌋\nRationale: Unexpected calls to LinIf_RxIndication shall be ignored.\n[SWS_LinIf_00849] ⌈If development error detection is enabled and an invalid value\nfor Channel is given, the function LinIf_RxIndication shall report LINIF_E_-\nNONEXISTENT_CHANNEL to the default error tracer.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00850] ⌈If development error detection is enabled and the parameter\nLin_SduPtr has an invalid value, the function LinIf_RxIndication shall raise the\ndevelopment error code LINIF_E_PARAM_POINTER.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00864] ⌈The function LinIf_RxIndication is only available if the LinIf\nmodule is configured as LIN slave node on at least one channel. In a pure LIN master\nconfiguration, this function is not available. This depends on the configuration parame-\nter LinIfNodeType.⌋"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.3.4 LinIf_TxConfirmation\nThe callback function LinIf_TxConfirmation is only applicable for LIN slave node.\n[SWS_LinIf_91006] Definition of callback function LinIf_TxConfirmation ⌈\nService Name\nLinIf_TxConfirmation\nSyntax\nvoid LinIf_TxConfirmation (\nNetworkHandleType Channel\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x7a\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant for different Channels. Non reentrant for the same Channel.\n▽\n△\nParameters (in)\nChannel\nIdentification of the LIN channel\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nNone\nDescription\nThe LIN Driver will call this function to report a successfully transmitted response. This function\nis only applicable for LIN slave nodes (available only if the ECU has any LIN slave channel).\nAvailable via\nLinIf.h\n⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00852] ⌈If no header of a transmit frame has been indicated before (no re-\nsponse transmission is expected), the function LinIf_TxConfirmation shall return\nwithout further action.⌋\nRationale: Unexpected calls to LinIf_TxConfirmation shall be ignored.\n[SWS_LinIf_00853] ⌈If development error detection is enabled and an invalid value\nfor Channel is given, the function LinIf_TxConfirmation shall report LINIF_E_\nNONEXISTENT_CHANNEL to the default error tracer.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00865] ⌈The function LinIf_TxConfirmation is only available if the\nLinIf module is configured as LIN slave node on at least one channel. In a pure LIN\nmaster configuration, this function is not available. This depends on the configuration\nparameter LinIfNodeType.⌋"

      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_LINTransceiverDriver",
      "source_page": 30,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",

      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "8.3.6 LinTrcv_CheckWakeup\n[SWS_LinTrcv_00012] Definition of callback function LinTrcv_CheckWakeup\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00310, SRS_BSW_00369, SRS_BSW_00375, SRS_BSW_\n00406\n⌈\nService Name\nLinTrcv_CheckWakeup\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType LinTrcv_CheckWakeup (\nuint8 LinNetwork\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x07\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant\nParameters (in)\nLinNetwork\nLIN network to which API call has to be applied.\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: API call has been accepted\nE_NOT_OK: API call has not been accepted\nDescription\nNotifies the calling function if a wakeup is detected.\nAvailable via\nLinTrcv.h\n⌋\n[SWS_LinTrcv_00144] ⌈If development error detection for the module LinTrcv is en-\nabled:\nIf called before the LinTrcv module has been initialized, the function LinTrcv_Check-\nWakeup shall report the development error LINTRCV_E_UNINIT.⌋\n[SWS_LinTrcv_00145] ⌈If development error detection for the module LinTrcv is en-\nabled:\nIf called with an invalid network number LinNetwork, the function LinTrcv_Check-\nWakeup shall report the development error LINTRCV_E_INVALID_LIN_NETWORK.⌋\n[SWS_LinTrcv_00166] ⌈The function LinTrcv_CheckWakeup shall evaluate the\nwakeup on the addressed LIN network.\nWhen a wake-up event on the addressed\nLIN network is detected (e.g. dominant bus state or negative edge at wakeup pin), the\nfunction LinTrcv_CheckWakeup shall notify the ECU State Manager module immedi-\nately via the EcuM_SetWakeupEvent and LinIf via LinIf_WakeupConfirmation callback\nfunction.⌋\n[SWS_LinTrcv_00167] ⌈If development error detection for the module LinTrcv is en-\nabled: If the addressed LIN network is not in mode LINTRCV_TRCV_MODE_SLEEP,\nthe function LinTrcv_CheckWakeup shall report the development error LINTRCV_\nE_TRCV_NOT_SLEEP.⌋\nConfiguration: See configuration parameter LinTrcvWakeUpSupport."
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.4.1 LinIf_MainFunction_<LinIfChannel.ShortName>\n[SWS_LinIf_00384] Definition of scheduled function LinIf_MainFunction_<LinIf\nChannel.ShortName>\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00373, SRS_Lin_01546, SRS_Lin_01561, SRS_Lin_01555\n⌈\nService Name\nLinIf_MainFunction_<LinIfChannel.ShortName>\nSyntax\nvoid LinIf_MainFunction_<LinIfChannel.ShortName> (\nvoid\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x80\nDescription\nThe main processing function of the LIN Interface.\nAvailable via\nSchM_LinIf.h\n⌋\nDesign hint: The function LinIf_MainFunction_<LinIfChannel.ShortName>\nmay be interrupted by other LIN Interface functions. Critical areas that are also modi-\nfied by other functions shall be protected. Other LIN Interface API calls that may touch\nthe same resources are the LinIf_GotoSleep, LinIf_Transmit, LinIf_Sched-\nuleRequest and LinIf_Wakeup, and potentially also LinIf_Init, LinTp_Init\nand LinTp_Shutdown.\n[SWS_LinIf_00725]\n⌈The\nfunction\nLinIf_MainFunction_<LinIfChannel.-\nShortName> shall exist once per LIN channel of the LIN Interface module.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00726] ⌈The function name of each instance of the LinIf MainFunc-\ntion shall be LinIf_MainFunction_<LinIfChannel.ShortName> where <Lin-\nIfChannel.ShortName> corresponds to the Short Name of the respective LIN chan-\nnel (LinIfChannel).⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00473]\n⌈The\nfunction\nLinIf_MainFunction_<LinIfChannel.-\nShortName> shall operate per LIN channel of the LIN Interface module.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00286]\n⌈The\nfunction\nLinIf_MainFunction_<LinIfChannel.-\nShortName> shall poll the Schedule Table Manager which frame shall be transported.\nThis requirement is only applicable to LIN master nodes.⌋\n[SWS_LinIf_00287] ⌈Only the function LinIf_MainFunction_<LinIfChannel.-\nShortName> shall process the transportation (transmission and reception) of frames.\nThis requirement is only applicable to LIN master nodes.⌋"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.5.3.5 Callout definitions\n8.5.3.5.1\n<User_ResponseErrorSignalChanged>\nThe callout function <User_ResponseErrorSignalChanged> is only applicable for\nLIN slave node.\n[SWS_LinIf_00856] Definition of configurable interface <User_ResponseError\nSignalChanged> ⌈\nService Name\n<User_ResponseErrorSignalChanged>\nSyntax\nvoid <User_ResponseErrorSignalChanged> (\nNetworkHandleType Channel,\nboolean RespErrSigValue\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x74\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant for different Channels. Non reentrant for the same Channel.\nChannel\nIdentification of the LIN channel.\nParameters (in)\nRespErrSigValue\nCurrent value of the response error signal. True if the signal is set\nto 1, false otherwise.\nOnly applicable for LIN slave nodes.\nParameters (inout)\nNone\n▽\n△\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nNone\nDescription\nNotifies the change of the response error signal with the new value.\nOnly applicable for LIN slave nodes.\nAvailable via\nLinIf_Externals.h\n⌋\nThis callout is optional, see [SWS_LinIf_00766].\nConfiguration of <User_ResponseErrorSignalChanged>: The name of the API\n<User_ResponseErrorSignalChanged> which will be called by the LIN Interface\nmodule shall be configured for the LIN Interface module by parameter LinIfRespon-\nseErrorSignalChangedCallout.\n8.5.3.5.2\n<User_SaveConfigurationRequest>\nThe callout function <User_SaveConfigurationRequest> is only applicable for\nLIN slave       "verbatim_text": "8.5.3 Configurable interfaces\nIn this section, all interfaces are listed, where the target function of any upper layer to\nbe called has to be set up by configuration. The specific call-out notification is specified in\nthe corresponding SWS document (see Chapter 3 “Related documentation”).\nAs far the interface name is not specified to be mandatory, no call-out is performed, if\nno API name is configured. This section describes only the content of notification of\nthe call-out, the call context inside the LIN Interface and exact time by the call event.\n<User>_NotificationName – This condition is applied for such interface services\nthat will be implemented in the upper layer (‘user’) and called by the LIN Interface. This\ncondition displays the symbolic name of the functional group in a call-out service in\nthe corresponding upper layer.       "verbatim_text": "8.6.1 Mandatory interfaces\nThis section defines all interfaces, which are required to fulfill the core functionality of\nthe module.\n[SWS_Lin_00234] Definition of mandatory interfaces in module Lin ⌈\nAPI Function\nHeader File\nDescription\nDem_SetEventStatus\nDem.h\nCalled by SW-Cs or BSW modules to report monitor\nstatus information to the Dem. BSW modules calling\nDem_SetEventStatus can safely ignore the return\nvalue. This API will be available only if ({Dem/Dem\nConfigSet/DemEventParameter/DemEvent\nReportingType} == STANDARD_REPORTING)\nEcuM_SetWakeupEvent\nEcuM.h\nSets the wakeup event.\nLinIf_WakeupConfirmation\nLinIf.h\nThe LIN Driver or LIN Transceiver Driver will call this\nfunction to report the wake up source after the\nsuccessful wakeup detection during CheckWakeup\nor after power on by bus.\n⌋()"

      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "8.6.2 Optional interfaces\nThis section defines all interfaces, which are required to fulfill an optional functionality\nof the module.\n[SWS_Lin_00235] Definition of optional interfaces requested by module Lin ⌈\nAPI Function\nHeader File\nDescription\nDet_ReportError\nDet.h\nService to report development errors.\nEcuM_CheckWakeup\nEcuM.h\nThis function can be called to check the given\nwakeup sources. It will pass the argument to the\nintegrator function EcuM_CheckWakeupHook. It can\nalso be called by the ISR of a wakeup source to set\nup the PLL and check other wakeup sources that\nmay be connected to the same interrupt.\nIcu_DisableNotification\nIcu.h\nThis function disables the notification of a channel.\nIcu_EnableNotification\nIcu.h\nThis function enables the notification on the given\nchannel.\nLinIf_HeaderIndication\nLinIf.h\nThe LIN Driver will call this function to report a\nreceived LIN header. This function is only applicable\nfor LIN slave nodes (available only if the ECU has\nany LIN slave channel).\nLinIf_LinErrorIndication\nLinIf.h\nThe LIN Driver will call this function to report a\ndetected error event during header or response\nprocessing. This function is only applicable for LIN\nslave nodes (available only if the ECU has any LIN\nslave channel).\nLinIf_RxIndication\nLinIf.h\nThe LIN Driver will call this function to report a\nsuccessfully received response and provides the\nreception data to the LIN Interface. This function is\nonly applicable for LIN slave nodes (available only if\nthe ECU has any LIN slave channel).\nLinIf_TxConfirmation\nLinIf.h\nThe LIN Driver will call this function to report a\nsuccessfully transmitted response. This function is\nonly applicable for LIN slave nodes (available only if\nthe ECU has any LIN slave channel).\n⌋\n[SWS_Lin_00176] ⌈The Lin module shall invoke the callback function EcuM_Check\nWakeup from within the wake-up ISR of the corresponding LIN channel when a valid\nLIN wake-up pulse has been detected.⌋\nRestrictions:\nA wake-up ISR can only be raised if supported by the LIN hardware (with or without\nIcu; up to the LIN driver implementation and the LIN hardware design). Therefore, Ecu\nM_CheckWakeup is supported if at least for one channel wake-up is supported (see\nconfiguration parameter LinChannelWakeupSupport)."
    },

      "verbatim_text": "9.1.2 Frame transmission in slave nodes\nThis section is only applicable to LIN slave nodes.\nThe following use case (Figure 9.3) shows the transmission of a LIN frame.\nAfter\na received LIN header is indicated by the LIN driver, the PID is evaluated (shown by\nfunction EvaluatePID). If it’s determined to belong to a transmission frame, the trans-\nmission response data is requested from upper layer. The buffer to which SduPtr\nmember in PduPtr parameter points to can be directly passed to let the upper layer\ncopy the transmission data to the provided buffer. The LIN interface informs the driver\nabout the response type by setting the appropriate members of PduPtr (shown by\nfunction SetPduPtrValues).\nThe CopyBuffer call is to show that the copying of the SDU is made in the LIN Driver\nand not in the LIN Interface.\n«module»\nLSduR\n«module»\nLin\n«module»\nLinIf\n«Peripheral»\nLinController/UART\nLSduR_LinIfTxConfirmation()\nLinIf_TxConfirmation()\nInterrupt()\nSetPduPtrValues()\nLinIf_HeaderIndication()\nLSduR_LinIfTriggerTransmit()\nInterrupt()\nCopyBuffer()\nEvaluatePID()\nSetupBuffer()\nFigure 9.3: Frame transmission (slave node)"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "9.1.2 LIN Slave\n«Peripheral»\nLinController/UART\n«module»\nLin\nUser\nalt Hardware support\n[Hardware LIN Controller]\n[Simple UART]\nloop Per received byte\nopt Last byte received\nInterrupt()\n[If HW Buffer is not accessible from\nCOM]:Copy Data from Hardware to\nframe buffer in RAM()\nLinIf_RxIndication(Lin_SduPtr)\n[Complete frame for this ECU has\nbeen received]:Set flag()\nInterrupt()\nLinIf_RxIndication(Lin_SduPtr)\nCopy byte from UART Hardware to buffer()\nFigure 9.2: LIN Frame Receiving Sequence Chart for LIN Slave"

      "verbatim_text": "9.2.2 Frame reception in slave nodes\nThis section is only applicable to LIN slave nodes.\nThe following use case (Figure 9.5) shows the reception of a LIN frame. After a re-\nceived LIN header is indicated by the LIN driver, the PID is evaluated (shown by func-\ntion EvaluatePID). If it’s determined to belong to a reception frame, the LIN inter-\nface informs the driver about the response type by setting the appropriate members of\nPduPtr (shown by function SetPduPtrValues).\nThe AllocateRxBuffer call is to show that the storage of the received frame is made\nin the LIN Driver and not in the LIN Interface.\n«module»\nLSduR\n«module»\nLin\n«module»\nLinIf\n«Peripheral»\nLinController/UART\nLin_Interrupt()\nCopyBuffer()\nLSduR_LinIfRxIndication()\nLinIf_RxIndication()\nLinIf_HeaderIndication()\nSetPduPtrValues()\nEvaluatePID()\nLin_Interrupt()\nAllocateRxBuffer()\nFigure 9.5: Frame reception (slave node)"

      "verbatim_text": "9.2.5 FlexRay Wakeup Sequences\nFor FlexRay a wake up is only possible via the FlexRay transceivers. There are two\ntransceivers for the two different channels in a FlexRay cluster. They are treated as\nbelonging to one network and thus, there should be only one wake up source identifier\nconfigured for both channels. Figure 9.11 shows the FlexRay transceiver wakeup via\ninterrupt. The interrupt is usually handled by the ICU Driver as described in Chapter\n9.2.2.\n«Peripheral»\nFlexRay       "verbatim_text": "9.3.2 Irrelevant communication in slave nodes\nThis section is only applicable to LIN slave nodes.\nThe third direction for a LIN frame is that the frame is not relevant for the slave node\nand is ignored. After a received LIN header is indicated by the LIN driver, the PID\nis evaluated (shown by function EvaluatePID). If it’s determined to belong to an\nIrrelevant frame, the LIN interface informs the driver about the response type by\nsetting the appropriate members of PduPtr (shown by function SetPduPtrValues).\nNo further action is made (Figure 9.7).\n«module»\nLin\n«module»\nLinIf\n«Peripheral»\nLinController/UART\nSetPduPtrValues()\nLin_Interrupt()\nLinIf_HeaderIndication()\nEvaluatePID()\nFigure 9.7: Irrelevant communication (slave node)"

      "verbatim_text": "9.4 Sporadic frame (Master only)\nThis section is only applicable to LIN master nodes. For LIN slave nodes, Sporadic\nframes are handled like reception of Unconditional frames.\nThe following use case (Figure 9.8) shows an upper layer requesting transmission of\na Sporadic frame. Actually, this call does not initiate the transmission of the frame\nsince the schedule table must be followed. It just marks the frame for transmission.\nWhen the Sporadic slot (note that the schedule entry for a Sporadic frame is\na slot and not a frame) is due in the schedule table, the LinIf_MainFunction_\n<LinIfChannel.ShortName> transmits the Sporadic frame as a normal trans-\nmitted frame and according to the priority rules for Sporadic frames.\nThe CheckId function is to show that the LIN Interface must check what frame is\npassed (convert the ID from the upper layer to the correct PID) from the upper layer.\nThe SetFlag function is a local function to flag the Sporadic frame for transmission\nin the LIN Interface. There is one flag for each Sporadic frame.\n«module»\nLSduR\n«module»\nLinIf\nLinIf_Transmit()\nCheckId()\nSetFlag()\nFigure 9.8: Sporadic frame (master node)"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "9.5.2 Event-triggered frame in slave nodes\nThis section is only applicable to LIN slave nodes.\nThe following use case (Figure 9.12) shows an upper layer requesting transmission\nof an Event-triggered frame. It just marks the frame for transmission. When\nthe header of the Event-triggered frame is received for which the associated\nresponse is pending, the transmission is requested from upper layer like for an uncon-\nditional transmission frame.\nThe CheckId function is to show that the LIN Interface must check what frame is\npassed (convert the ID from the upper layer to the correct PID) from the upper layer.\nThe SetFlag function is a local function to flag the Event-triggered frame for\ntransmission in the LIN Interface.\nThere is one flag for each Event-triggered\nframe.\nThe CopyPID function is to show that that the LIN Interface must copy the PID of the\nrequested Event-triggered frame to the first byte of the payload data.\nThe ClearFlag function is a local function to clear the pending flag of an Event-\ntriggered frame after successful transmission.\n«module»\nLSduR\n«module»\nLin\n«module»\nLinIf\nLinIf_TxConfirmation()\nCopyPID()\nLSduR_LinIfTriggerTransmit()\nSetupBuffer()\nLSduR_LinIfTxConfirmation()\nSetFlag()\nLinIf_HeaderIndication()\nLinIf_Transmit()\nCheckId()\nEvaluatePID()\nClearFlag()\nFigure 9.12: Event-triggered frame (slave node)"
    },

      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "9.6 Transport Protocol message transmission\nThe following diagram (Figure 9.13) shows the transmission of a TP message. The\ninitiation of the message, the continuous copying of the data and the finish of the mes-\nsage are shown. The actual transmission of the MRF/SRF is not shown in the diagram\nand it has the same behavior as frame transmission.\nThe TP message start is always initiated by requesting to send the TP message from\nthe PDU Router. For LIN master nodes, the schedule table change to the diagnostic re-\nquest schedule is requested if a schedule table change is enabled by the configuration\nparameter (see the parameter LinTpScheduleChangeDiag).\nThe TP message is finished after the last N-PDU (SF or CF) is transmitted. The PDU\nRouter is notified of the completion of the message transmission.\nFor LIN master\nnodes, the schedule table change to the diagnostic response schedule is requested if\na schedule table change is enabled by the configuration parameter (see the parameter\nLinTpScheduleChangeDiag).\n«module»\nLinIf\nBSW Task (OS task\nor cyclic call)\n«module»\nPduR\n«module»\nBswM\n«module»\nLinSM\nalt TP status\n[Starting TP message]\n[TP message transmission]\n[Ending TP message]\nloop\nopt Schedule table change is enabled\nopt Schedule table change is enabled\nPduR_LinTpTxConfirmation()\nLinIf_MainFunction_<ChannelId>()\nBswM_LinTp_RequestMode()\nLinIf_MainFunction_<ChannelId>()\nPduR_LinTpCopyTxData()\nLinIf_ScheduleRequest()\nLinSM_ScheduleRequest()\nLinTp_Transmit()\nBswM_LinTp_RequestMode()\nLinIf_ScheduleRequest()\nLinSM_ScheduleRequest()\nFigure 9.13: Transport Protocol message transmission"

      "verbatim_text": "10.3.5 LinSMSchedule\n[ECUC_LinSM_00146] Definition of EcucParamConfContainerDef LinSMSched-\nule ⌈\nContainer Name\nLinSMSchedule\nParent Container\nLinSMChannel\nDescription\nThe schedule references to a schedule that is located in the LinIf configuration.\nMoreover, the PDU groups are located in the COM configuration. Note that there are\ntwo references to PDU groups. The simple reason is that a PDU group is only allowed\nto contain one direction (TX or RX). Only applicable to LIN master nodes.\nMultiplicity\n0..*\nConfiguration Parameters\nIncluded Parameters\nParameter Name\nMultiplicity\nECUC ID\nLinSMScheduleIndex\n1\n[ECUC_LinSM_00001]\nLinSMScheduleIndexRef\n1\n[ECUC_LinSM_00149]\nNo Included Containers\n⌋\n[ECUC_LinSM_00001] Definition of EcucIntegerParamDef LinSMScheduleIndex\n⌈\nParameter Name\nLinSMScheduleIndex\nParent Container\nLinSMSchedule\nDescription\nThis index parameter can be used by the BswM as a SymbolicNameReference target.\nThe LinSM just forwards the request from the BswM to LinIf. Note that the value of the\nLinSMScheduleIndex shall be the same as the value from the LinIf.\nMultiplicity"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "6 Requirements Tracing\nThe following tables reference the requirements specified in [3] and [9] and links to the\nfulfillment of these. Please note that if column “Satisfied by” is empty for a specific\nrequirement this means that this requirement is not fulfilled by this document.\nRequirement\nDescription\nSatisfied by\n[SRS_BSW_00004]\nAll Basic SW Modules shall perform a\npre-processor check of the versions\nof all imported include files\n[SWS_LinSM_00208]\n[SRS_BSW_00101]\nThe Basic Software Module shall be\nable to initialize variables and\nhardware in a separate initialization\nfunction\n[SWS_LinSM_00155]\n[SRS_BSW_00167]\nAll AUTOSAR Basic Software\nModules shall provide configuration\nrules and constraints to enable\nplausibility checks\n[SWS_LinSM_00073]\n[SRS_BSW_00358]\nThe return type of init() functions\nimplemented by AUTOSAR Basic\nSoftware Modules shall be void\n[SWS_LinSM_00155]\n[SRS_BSW_00369]\nAll AUTOSAR Basic Software\nModules shall not return specific\ndevelopment error codes via the API\n[SWS_LinSM_00113] [SWS_LinSM_00122]\n[SWS_LinSM_00126]\n[SRS_BSW_00373]\nThe main processing function of each\nAUTOSAR Basic Software Module\nshall be named according the defined\nconvention\n[SWS_LinSM_00156]\n[SRS_BSW_00384]\nThe Basic Software Module\nspecifications shall specify at least in\nthe description which other modules\nthey require\n[SWS_LinSM_00001] [SWS_LinSM_00085]\n[SWS_LinSM_00086] [SWS_LinSM_00105]\n[SWS_LinSM_00196]\n[SRS_BSW_00406]\nAPI handling in uninitialized state\n[SWS_LinSM_00116] [SWS_LinSM_00125]\n[SWS_LinSM_00128] [SWS_LinSM_00131]\n[SWS_LinSM_00134] [SWS_LinSM_00137]\n[SRS_BSW_00407]\nEach BSW module shall provide a\nfunction to read out the version\ninformation of a dedicated module\nimplementation\n[SWS_LinSM_00117]\n[SRS_BSW_00414]\nInit functions shall have a pointer to a\nconfiguration structure as single\nparameter\n[SWS_LinSM_00155]\nTable 6.1: Requirements Tracing"
    },

      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "7.1.1 LINSM_UNINIT\nThe uninit state is the first state that is active in the LinSM module.\n[SWS_LinSM_00022] ⌈There shall be a state called LINSM_UNINIT⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00161] ⌈The state LINSM_UNINIT shall be active at start-up, before\nany API is called.⌋"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_LINSM_SECTION_7_1_3_LINSM_NO_COM",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_LINStateManager",
      "source_page": 23,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "7.1.3 LINSM_NO_COM\nThe no communication state is active after initialization and when the ComM module\nrequests no communication (LIN master node) or when the LinIf indicates a bus sleep\nevent (LIN slave node).\n[SWS_LinSM_00026] ⌈There shall be a sub-state called LINSM_NO_COM in the state\nLINSM_INIT.⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00027] ⌈When entering LINSM_NO_COM the LinSM module shall no-\ntify (with the exception [SWS_LinSM_00166]) ComM of the state change by calling the\nComM_BusSM_ModeIndication with the parameter COMM_NO_COMMUNICATION\nfor the specific network.⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00193] ⌈When entering LINSM_NO_COM the LinSM module shall no-\ntify (with the exception [SWS_LinSM_00166]) BswM of the state change by calling the\nBswM_LinSM_CurrentState with the parameter LINSM_NO_COM for the specific net-\nwork.⌋\nThere is one exception to the above two requirements. The rationale is that the ComM\nmay not be initialized when executing the LinSM_Init function.\n[SWS_LinSM_00166] ⌈The LinSM module shall not notify the state change to LINSM_\nNO_COM when the LinSM is executing the LinSM_Init function, i.e. the LinSM_Init\nfunction shall neither call ComM_BusSM_ModeIndication nor BswM_LinSM_Current\nState.⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00028] ⌈When LINSM_NO_COM is active, the LinSM module shall not\ncommand the LinIf module to communicate for the selected network, i.e. bus shall be\nsilent.\nNote: Upon entering or exiting the LINSM_NO_COM state the LinSM module will not\nset the hardware interface or µ-controller into a new power mode. This is not in the\nscope of the LinSM⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00203] ⌈When entering LINSM_NO_COM the transceiver shall be set\nto STANDBY if LinSMTransceiverPassiveMode is true and SLEEP otherwise by using\nthe LinIf_SetTrcvMode. This requirement is applicable only when LinSMTransceiver\nPassiveMode is configured for the channel.⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00204] ⌈The LinIf_SetTrcvMode shall not be called from the function\nLinSM_Init.\nNote: There is no need to set the mode in the LinSM init function since the Transceiver\nwill set the mode in its init function. The mode is selected in the Transceiver configura-\ntion.⌋"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_LINSM_SECTION_7_1_4_LINSM_FULL_COM",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_LINStateManager",
      "source_page": 23,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "7.1.4 LINSM_FULL_COM\nThe LINSM_FULL_COM is the only state where communication on the LIN bus is al-\nlowed. Each network can be in LINSM_FULL_COM independent of each other. All of\nthe following requirements are applicable for each network.\n[SWS_LinSM_00032] ⌈There shall be a sub-state called LINSM_FULL_COM for each\nnetwork in the state LINSM_INIT.⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00033] ⌈When entering LINSM_FULL_COM the ComM shall be noti-\nfied of the state change by calling the ComM_BusSM_ModeIndication with the param-\neter COMM_FULL_COMMUNICATION for the specified network.⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00192] ⌈When entering LINSM_FULL_COM the BswM shall be noti-\nfied of the state change by calling the BswM_LinSM_CurrentState with the parameter\nLINSM_FULL_COM for the specified network.⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00205] ⌈When entering LINSM_FULL_COM the transceiver shall be\nset to active by using the LinIf_SetTrcvMode. This requirement is applicable only when\nLinSMTransceiverPassiveMode is configured for the channel.⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00301] ⌈When entering LINSM_FULL_COM, the sub-state LINSM_\nRUN_COMMUNICATION will be entered.⌋"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_LINSM_SECTION_7_1_8_Timeout_of_requests",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_LINStateManager",
      "source_page": 28,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "7.1.8 Timeout of requests\nAfter calling LinIf_Wakeup the LinSM module is waiting for the LinIf module to confirm\nthe wake up on the bus. There is a possibility that the confirmation is not received, and\ntherefore the LinSM module will wait forever.\nThe cause for a missing wakeup confirmation could be a problem in software, but also\na bus failure or a problem in the master node. A slave node confirms a bus wakeup not\nafter wakeup transmission like a master node, but with reception of the first LIN header\nfrom the master node. A LIN slave node shall repeat the wakeup frame transmission up\nto three times if the communication does not start. After three (failing) wakeup requests\nthe node shall wait a minimum time before restarting the wake up process.\n[SWS_LinSM_00175] ⌈There shall be independent wakeup confirmation timers for\neach network.⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00162] ⌈The (countdown and expiration) handling of wakeup confirma-\ntion timers shall be done in the LinSM_MainFunction.⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00159] ⌈The wakeup confirmation timeout parameter LinSMConfirma-\ntionTimeout shall have a time that is either 0 or divisible by the LinSM_MainFunction\n(i.e. LinSM_MainFunction period * m; m integer >0).⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00100] ⌈Before the LinSM calls LinIf_Wakeup on a channel it shall start\na wakeup confirmation timer for the according channel with the configured timeout\nparameter LinSMConfirmationTimeout if LinSMConfirmationTimeout > 0.⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00154] ⌈If LinSM_WakeupConfirmation is called on a channel before\nthe wakeup confirmation timer has expired on the according channel LinSM shall stop\nthe timer.⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00102] ⌈If a wakeup confirmation timer elapses (i.e. no wakeup con-\nfirmation occurred) and the maximum number of retries (LinSMModeRequestRepeti-\ntionMax) has been reached and LinSMDevErrorDetect (ECUC_LinSM_00206) is set to\nTRUE, the LinSM module shall report LINSM_E_CONFIRMATION_TIMEOUT to DET.⌋\nMaking the timeout optional enhances implementation size, if the timeout is not re-\nquired:\nNote: If the configuration parameter LinSMConfirmationTimeout is set to zero the\nwakeup confirmation timer is not used, and hence a timeout cannot occur. This means\nthat requirement [SWS_LinSM_00102] will not happen.\n[SWS_LinSM_00304] ⌈If a wakeup confirmation timer elapses (i.e. no wakeup con-\nfirmation occurred), LinSMNodeType is set to MASTER and ComM request is still\nCOMM_FULL_COMMUNICATION then LinIf_Wakeup shall be called.⌋\nNote:\nLinSM stops to retry when confirmation callback LinSM_WakeupConfirma-\ntion (SWS_LinSM_00132) occurs or timeout parameter LinSMConfirmationTimeout\n(ECUC_LinSM_00144) is expired and ComM requests COMM_NO_COMMUNICA-\nTION.\n[SWS_LinSM_00235] ⌈If a wakeup confirmation timer elapses (i.e. no wakeup con-\nfirmation occurred), the maximum number of retries (LinSMModeRequestRepetition\nMax) has not been reached, LinSMNodeType is set to Slave and ComM request is still\nCOMM_FULL_COMMUNICATION then LinIf_Wakeup shall be called.⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00236] ⌈If a wakeup confirmation timer elapses (i.e. no wakeup con-\nfirmation occurred), the maximum number of retries (LinSMModeRequestRepetition\nMax) has been reached, LinSMNodeType is set to Slave then LinSM shall wait the\nsilence-after-wakeup time (LinSMSilenceAfterWakeupTimeout) and afterwards restart\nthe wakeup process by\n• calling LinIf_Wakeup if ComM request is still COMM_FULL_COMMUNICATION.\n• resetting the counter for maximum number of retries.\n⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00237] ⌈If a wakeup confirmation timer elapses (i.e. no wakeup confir-\nmation occurred), the maximum number of retries (LinSMModeRequestRepetitionMax)\nhas been reached, LinSMNodeType is set to Slave, the silence-after-wakeup time (Lin\nSMSilenceAfterWakeupTimeout) has not expired and ComM requests COMM_FULL_\nCOMMUNICATION then the call of LinIf_Wakeup shall be delayed to the expiration of\nthe silence-after-wakeup time.⌋"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_LINSM_SECTION_7_2_Handling_multiple_networks_and_drivers",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_LINStateManager",
      "source_page": 28,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "7.2 Handling multiple networks and drivers\nUsually only one LIN driver module (supporting multiple networks) is needed in an\nECU to handle all LIN networks. However, rarely, some hardware configurations the\nECU contain different LIN hardware (e.g. an advanced LIN controller and a UART). In\nsuch case, more than one different LIN drivers are required. This will not affect the Lin\nSM module since the LIN driver only interfaces the LinIf module and not the LIN driver\nmodule directly.\nThe LinSM will only handle networks, and is not concerned to which driver the network\nmaps to, this will be handled by the LinIf."
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.3.2 LinSM_ScheduleRequest\nThe service LinSM_ScheduleRequest is only applicable for LIN master node.\n[SWS_LinSM_00113] Definition of API function LinSM_ScheduleRequest\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00369\n⌈\nService Name\nLinSM_ScheduleRequest\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType LinSM_ScheduleRequest (\nNetworkHandleType network,\nLinIf_SchHandleType ScheduleTableIdx\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x10\nSync/Async\nAsynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant\nnetwork\nIdentification of the LIN channel\nParameters (in)\nScheduleTableIdx\nIndex of the scheduled table\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK - Schedule table request has been accepted.\nE_NOT_OK - Not possible to perform the request, e.g. not\ninitialized.\nDescription\nThe upper layer requests a schedule table to be changed on one LIN network.\nAvailable via\nLinSM.h\n⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00114] ⌈If LinSMDevErrorDetect is enabled: If the network parameter\nhas an invalid value then the error-code LINSM_E_NONEXISTENT_NETWORK shall\nbe reported to the DET module and E_NOT_OK shall be returned.⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00115] ⌈If LinSMDevErrorDetect is enabled: If the schedule parameter\nhas an invalid value, then the error-code LINSM_E_PARAMETER shall be reported to\nthe DET module and E_NOT_OK shall be returned.⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00116]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00406\n⌈If LinSMDevErrorDetect is enabled: If the state LINSM_UNINIT is active then the\nerror-code LINSM_E_UNINIT shall be reported to the DET module and E_NOT_OK\nshall be returned.⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_10211] ⌈If the function LinSM_ScheduleRequest is called and the state\nis not LINSM_FULL_COM, the LinSM_ScheduleRequest shall return directly with E_\nNOT_OK.⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00163] ⌈If the function LinSM_ScheduleRequest is called, LinSMOver-\nwritePendingScheduleRequestProcessing is set to FALSE and another schedule re-\nquest on the same network is pending, the LinSM_ScheduleRequest shall return di-\nrectly with E_NOT_OK.⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00165] ⌈If the function LinSM_ScheduleRequest is called, LinSMOver-\nwritePendingScheduleRequestProcessing is set to TRUE and another schedule re-\nquest on the same network is pending, the pending schedule request shall be overwrit-\nten with the new schedule request and return with E_OK.⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00241] ⌈The function LinSM_ScheduleRequest shall be available if the\nLinSM module is configured as LIN master node on at least one channel.⌋\nNote: In a pure LIN slave configuration, this function is not available. This depends on\nthe configuration parameters LinSMNodeType."
    },

Non reentrant for the same network.\nParameters (in)\nnetwork\nHandle of the communication channel\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nmode\nPointer to the memory location where the current communication\nmode shall be stored\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: Request accepted\nE_NOT_OK: Request not accepted\nDescription\nQuery the current communication mode.\nAvailable via\nLinSM.h\n⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00123] ⌈If LinSMDevErrorDetect is enabled: If the network parameter\nhas an invalid value, then the error-code LINSM_E_NONEXISTENT_NETWORK shall\nbe reported to the DET module and E_NOT_OK shall be returned.⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00124] ⌈If LinSMDevErrorDetect is enabled: If the mode pointer param-\neter is invalid (e.g. NULL), then the error-code LINSM_E_PARAM_POINTER shall be\nreported to the DET module and E_NOT_OK shall be returned.⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00125]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00406\n⌈If LinSMDevErrorDetect is enabled: If the state LINSM_UNINIT is active, then the\nerror-code LINSM_E_UNINIT shall be reported to the DET module and E_NOT_OK\nshall be returned⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00180] ⌈If active state is LINSM_NO_COM the state COMM_NO_\nCOMMUNICATION shall be returned.⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00181] ⌈If active state is LINSM_FULL_COM the state COMM_FULL_\nCOMMUNICATION shall be returned.⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00182] ⌈If active state is LINSM_UNINIT the state COMM_NO_COM-\nMUNICATION shall be returned. This is also captured above when the DET is enabled.\nThis is to be defensive.⌋\nNote that COMM_SILENT_COMMUNICATION is not used by the LinSM module."

      "verbatim_text": "8.5.2 LinSM_GotoSleepIndication\nThe callback LinSM_GotoSleepIndication is only applicable for LIN slave node.\n[SWS_LinSM_91000] Definition of callback function LinSM_GotoSleepIndication\n⌈\nService Name\nLinSM_GotoSleepIndication\nSyntax\nvoid LinSM_GotoSleepIndication (\nNetworkHandleType Channel\n)\n▽\n△\nService ID [hex]\n0x03\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant for different Channels\nParameters (in)\nChannel\nIdentification of the LIN channel\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nNone\nDescription\nThe LinIf will call this callback when the go to sleep command is received on the network or a\nbus idle timeout occurs.\nOnly applicable for LIN slave nodes.\nAvailable via\nLinSM.h\n⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00239] ⌈If LinSMDevErrorDetect is enabled: If the network parameter\nhas an invalid value, then the error-code LINSM_E_NONEXISTENT_NETWORK shall\nbe reported to the DET module.⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00240] ⌈If LinSMDevErrorDetect is enabled:\nIf the state LINSM_\nUNINIT is active, then the error-code LINSM_E_UNINIT shall be reported to DET mod-\nule.⌋\n[SWS_LinSM_00243] ⌈The callback function LinSM_GotoSleepIndication shall be\navailable if the LinSM module is configured as LIN slave node on at least one channel.⌋\nNote: In a pure LIN master configuration, this function is not available. This depends\non the configuration parameters LinSMNodeType."

      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_LINTRCV_SECTION_7_2_LIN_transceiver_hardware_operation_modes",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_LINTransceiverDriver",
      "source_page": 16,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "7.2 LIN transceiver hardware operation modes\nThe LIN transceiver hardware may support more mode transitions than the software.\nThe dependencies and the recommended implementations behaviour are explained in\nthis chapter.\nIt is up to the implementation to decide which LIN transceiver hardware state is covered\nby which LIN transceiver driver software state. An implementation has to guarantee\nthat whole functionality of described LIN transceiver driver is given by the implementa-\ntion."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_LINTRCV_SECTION_7_4_LIN_transceiver_wakeup_modes",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_LINTransceiverDriver",
      "source_page": 17,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "7.4 LIN transceiver wakeup modes\n[SWS_LinTrcv_00066]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Lin_01514, SRS_Lin_01563\n⌈Wakeup notification must be supported by LIN Transceiver driver, therefore LIN\ntransceiver driver covers 2 wakeup modes, internal wakeup by an upper layer or exter-\nnal wakeup by LIN channel.⌋\n1. Internal wakeup: An internal wakeup is initiated by an upper layer, e.g. by calling\nLinTrcv_Init or LinTrcv_SetOpMode.\n2. External wakeup: Wakeup detected by LIN transceiver driver is forwarded to the\nupper layer through the API LinTrcv_CheckWakeup which has to be called by\nthe LinIf.\nHint: WakeUp through ISR is not supported by the LIN Transceiver Driver but is only\npossible through ICU.\n[SWS_LinTrcv_00074]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Lin_01580\n⌈Selection of wakeup mode shall be done by configuration parameter LinTrcvWake-\nUpSupport.⌋\n[SWS_LinTrcv_00075]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Lin_01580\n⌈Support of wakeup shall be switched on and off for each LIN transceiver channel\nindividually by configuration parameter LinTrcvWakeupByBusUsed.⌋\n[SWS_LinTrcv_00161] ⌈LinTrcv driver shall use the following APIs provided by ICU\ndriver, to enable and disable the wakeup event notification:\n• Icu_EnableNotification\n• Icu_DisableNotification\n⌋\n[SWS_LinTrcv_00162] ⌈LinTrcv driver shall enable the ICU channels when the\ntransceiver transmits to standby mode (LINTRCV_STANDBY)⌋\n[SWS_LinTrcv_00163] ⌈LinTrcv driver shall disable the ICU channels when the\ntransceiver transmits to Normal mode (LINTRCV_NORMAL)⌋\nRationale: LinTrcv driver shall avoid the loss of wakeup events."
    },
